about: Every character the x10 opening needs. ce_tag = the original biped tag (its animation graph has the same path). remake_meshes are the host game's own assets loaded by path at runtime; 'ce_model' placeholders are built at runtime from the player's MCC; 'none' = not drawn in this version (voice and camera still play). Nothing here ships game content. remake_meshes are assembled the way the remake's own BP_KeyesBipedActor is (read in game): part_parent = 1-based index of the mesh each part hangs off with no socket (0 = actor root), part_yaw = its relative yaw. attach_bone 'leader' means that scheme: parts are placed so in the body's rest pose, then the face (and what hangs off it) follows the body's Head_M. follow_bones: [body bone, face bone] pairs; the face (a MetaHuman mesh with its own full skeleton, so its neck skin is weighted to its own spine/neck bones) is posed each frame so those bones turn as the body's do, which keeps the neck seam closed. align_bones: [face bone, body bone] put at the same spot when Keyes is built (seen in game: the face sat low and forward, head sunk into the collar). voice_prefix: voice lines whose name contains it are this character's (his mouth moves with them). jaw: face bone candidates (first found is used), max opening in degrees and the loudness that opens it fully; the opening axis is his left-right axis, sign chosen so the chin goes down. tint: colour (0-1 RGB) put on the material's Color parameter for a ce_model stand-in. jaw.with: [name fragment, weight] for face bones carried round the jaw pivot with it (lips/teeth/tongue hang off the face root on this face). fallback 'h2a': drawn from the player's Halo 2 Anniversary files in their MCC (halo2\preload\paks\shared.pck) and posed by the original's animations for ce_tag; h2a: tpl = template, parts = submeshes drawn (1-based; the mouth pieces are left out), material = translucent unlit material with texture_param/tint_param, tint = RGBA, fallback_material + tint when that material is missing, scale = size drawn at (1 = life size, as the original shows her). part_leader: 1-based mesh whose pose each part follows (0 = posed itself / none): parts on the body's skeleton follow the body, hair and brows follow the face. variants: [[face, hair], ...] swapped in for meshes 2 and 3, picked per object by its name, so a crowd has different faces. h2a.scale: a number, or "ce" = drawn at the original model's height (CE Cortana is a ~55 cm hologram on a pedestal; the original's shots are framed for that). h2a.png_filter: ffmpeg filter that turns her texture into the original's violet glow (a floor keeps the dark suit from going black); png_suffix names that cache. floor: foot planting. from = cm above the posed feet the floor trace starts (300 = Keyes' approved 0.2.3 setting; crew 70, under consoles and railings); smooth = ease and reject >40 cm jumps; ignore_cast = the trace passes through the other spawned characters. borrow_graph: another character's original animation graph (same bip01 body) whose unarmed stand/alert idles and walks are used before the character's own armed ones (crewmen use the marine's graph, which only stands holding a pistol or rifle; they borrow the captain's empty-handed ones). "-" = none. h2a.use: "hologram" (textured translucent; drew black in game) or "tinted" (fallback_material in fallback_tint, the material the solid CE stand-in rendered with). bounds_scale: how much bigger each mesh part's visibility box is drawn. The box follows the standing reference pose; seated or running crew moved their head outside it, so the game stopped drawing the face when the camera looked down at them (and parts popped). 1 = unchanged (Keyes). uniforms: the remake's own NavyCrew division materials (Command, Engineer, Science: its red, yellow and blue), one picked per object by its name, put on the body and sleeves slots that wear the default uniform material. h2a.use "vertex": her texture tinted by vertex_filter (dark blue to light cyan, as her H2A hologram) sampled at each point and drawn with vertex_material (the engine vertex colour material); checked offline in devtools/render_cortana.py --holo. h2a.vertex_filter now violet (the original CE Cortana, reference/cortana_sheet.jpg). h2a.shimmer: hologram light on her painted colours each frame: base brightness, band = extra brightness of bands sweeping up (band_every cm apart, band_width cm, band_speed cm/s), scanline = depth of fine lines (scanline_freq rad/cm of rest height), flicker = brightness wobble.
